grammar.title: Grammatik
grammar.rule: Ich arbeite am Montag. → Am Montag arbeite ich. · Wir lesen im Laden. → Im Laden lesen wir.

tables.caption: am Montag · um zehn Uhr · im Laden
am Samstag · um zehn Uhr · eine Stunde

grammar.note_en:
German statements keep the finite verb in the second constituent position. The finite verb is the part that changes for its subject: arbeite with ich, arbeitet with Lina, arbeiten with wir. The first constituent is one whole unit, not necessarily one word. Compare Ich arbeite am Montag (“I work on Monday”) with Am Montag arbeite ich (“On Monday I work”). Am Montag is one time phrase; arbeite still comes second, then the subject ich. Do not leave the subject before the verb after moving a time phrase to the front.

The story repeatedly changes the first unit while keeping that pattern: Heute arbeiten wir auch (“Today we work too”), Um zehn Uhr lesen wir das Heft (“At ten o’clock we read the notebook”), and Im Laden lesen wir zusammen (“In the shop we read together”). A subject can still come first, and the verb remains second.

A known object can come first when it is the topic being contrasted or assigned: Den Schlüssel hat Lina (“Lina has the key”), Den Stuhl bringe ich (“I will bring the chair”), Das Heft liest Mira (“Mira reads the notebook”), Das Foto zeigt Lina (“Lina shows the photo”). This is not a change of subject or case: den Schlüssel and den Stuhl remain accusative objects; Lina and ich remain subjects. The context assigns different objects to different people, so the focus has a purpose. With das Heft the nominative and accusative forms look identical; who reads what comes from the known roles and the verb.

Names of weekdays are capitalized. Am Montag, am Dienstag, am Mittwoch, am Donnerstag, am Freitag, am Samstag and am Sonntag mean “on Monday” through “on Sunday.” Here am is the same contraction of an dem that you met in am Fenster, now used with a day rather than a place. Heute ist Freitag (“Today is Friday”) and Morgen ist Samstag (“Tomorrow is Saturday”) identify the story’s relative day; the calendar does not claim a specific real-world date. A Woche is a week, made up of sieben Tage (“seven days”); a Monat is a month, and a Jahr a year with zwölf Monate (“twelve months”). The calendar picture distinguishes a single day square, a seven-day week, a month panel and a whole year.

Um introduces a clock time: um sechs Uhr (“at six o’clock”), um sieben Uhr (“at seven”), um acht Uhr (“at eight”), um neun Uhr (“at nine”), um zehn Uhr (“at ten”), um elf Uhr (“at eleven”) and um zwölf Uhr (“at twelve”). Uhr also names a clock: eine Uhr (“a clock”). After a number in a clock expression, Uhr stays singular. These are whole morning hours; no evening-time numbers, ordinal dates or half-hour patterns are introduced. The new number words are six through twelve, with their numerical values shown on the clock and calendar aids.

Stunde means an hour as an interval, distinct from Uhr used in a clock time. The shared reading hour begins at ten and ends at eleven: Die Stunde endet um elf Uhr (“The hour ends at eleven o’clock”). Minute is a minute, shown by one step of the long hand between adjacent minute ticks, rather than a step of the short hand between hours. Wir warten eine Minute (“We wait one minute”) and Wir lesen eine Stunde zusammen (“We read together for an hour”) give the length of an activity. With two, use Minuten: zwei Minuten (“two minutes”). These duration phrases do not need um; um names a starting or ending clock time.

Früh and spät mean “early” and “late,” relative to the activity and the people. Six or seven is early for Nora’s child; twelve is too late for a common hour before Nora’s work. Ben can arrive early at eight and work in the house, then return at ten. Lina has the key and is expected to open the shop at ten after her morning work. Beginne is “I begin,” beginnen is “we/they begin,” and endet is “ends”; the story uses Wir beginnen (“We begin”) and Die Stunde endet (“The hour ends”). The neighbours agree one common hour. Ada has not promised to come: Emil only says he will ask her. The uncertain year on the old letter remains a different question from their definite Saturday plan.
